description: Current-law cross-reference and supersession notices for Pub. L. 42–274, the United States Capitol Police Reform and Accountability Act.

notes.heading: USAR 2026 Capitol Police Reform and Accountability Act
paragraphs: Pub. L. 42–274, §§ 4–8, establishes the current USAR Capitol Police organization and governance framework, including the United States Capitol Police, Capitol Police Board, Chief, directives, Deputy Chief, and Acting Chief. Those permanent provisions are editorially classified at 2 U.S.C. §§ 7002–7006.

Section 2 of Pub. L. 42–274 expressly repeals the Uniformed Capitol Police Act of 2023 and the United States Capitol Police Technical Corrections Act and supersedes inconsistent continuing law, rule, regulation, or order. This baseline section is retained as enacted historical text; to the extent of inconsistency, the later 2026 Act controls.

notes.heading: USAR 2026 Capitol Police Board Framework
paragraphs: Pub. L. 42–274, § 5, supplies the current USAR composition, voting, chairmanship, meeting, transparency, and oversight rules for the Capitol Police Board and is editorially classified at 2 U.S.C. § 7003.
The baseline Board provisions remain printed for statutory history, subject to the express repeal and inconsistency-supersession rule in Pub. L. 42–274, § 2.

notes.heading: USAR 2026 Capitol Police Jurisdiction and Congressional Control
paragraphs: Pub. L. 42–274, §§ 9–10, establishes the current USAR jurisdictional framework for the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds and allocates operational authority among the House Sergeant at Arms, Senate Sergeant at Arms, Capitol Police Board, Chief, and presiding officers. Those provisions are editorially classified at 2 U.S.C. §§ 7007–7008.
Related arrest, removal, detention, and force rules are classified at 2 U.S.C. §§ 7012–7013. The baseline text remains printed for statutory history subject to Pub. L. 42–274, § 2.

notes.heading: USAR 2026 Capitol Police Law-Enforcement Authority
paragraphs: Pub. L. 42–274, §§ 9, 14, and 15, governs current USAR Capitol Police jurisdiction, removals, temporary detentions, arrests, arrest reporting, and use of force. Those provisions are editorially classified at 2 U.S.C. §§ 7007, 7012, and 7013.
The baseline law-enforcement text remains printed as enacted history; the later framework controls to the extent Pub. L. 42–274, § 2, renders earlier authority inconsistent.

notes.heading: USAR 2026 Executive Noninterference and Interagency Assistance
paragraphs: Pub. L. 42–274, § 16, provides that the Capitol Police is a legislative-branch entity and bars Executive Branch direction, command, supervision, or control of its operations while preserving lawful requests for assistance, information sharing, protective coordination, and joint operations. That provision is editorially classified at 2 U.S.C. § 7014.
This section remains printed as baseline enacted text and is read subject to the later Act's express inconsistency-supersession clause.

notes.heading: USAR 2026 Capitol Police Special Officers
paragraphs: Pub. L. 42–274, § 13, authorizes the Chief, with approval of the Capitol Police Board, to appoint special officers for specified temporary or specialized duties and defines their scope and limitations. The provision is editorially classified at 2 U.S.C. § 7011.
The baseline special-officer text remains printed for statutory history subject to Pub. L. 42–274, § 2.

notes.heading: USAR 2026 Protective Services and Deployment Outside Capitol Grounds
paragraphs: Pub. L. 42–274, §§ 11–12, governs current USAR protective services and deployments outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, including authorization, purposes, coordination, command, duration, and reporting. Those provisions are editorially classified at 2 U.S.C. §§ 7009–7010.
The baseline deployment text remains printed for statutory history and is subject to the later Act's express repeal and inconsistency-supersession rule.
